title: Adaptive runtime versioning and fallback compatibility matrix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement an adaptive semantic versioning approach for the serving runtime that pairs explicit capability flags with a maintained fallback compatibility matrix and exposes a negotiation/fallback header for clients. This ticket defines the policy, the rollout gates, the matrix generation process, and the upgrade tool changes required to support zero-downtime client migrations.
background: Our current semver playbook focuses on human-driven release notes and manual migration shims. As model-serving surfaces increase and private deployments adopt pinned versions, we need an automated, machine-readable compatibility signal and a narrowly-scoped LTS mapping so clients can negotiate, fall back safely, and operators can reliably roll out upgrades with automated gates.
goals: 1) Define a runtime capability-first versioning policy that augments semver with feature flags; 2) Produce a canonical, machine-readable fallback compatibility matrix per release channel (stable/LTS/beta); 3) Introduce an HTTP Accept-Version-like negotiation header and server fallback semantics; 4) Extend the upgrade operator and migration CLI to consume the matrix and perform safe rollouts and automatic shim delivery.
non_goals: Rewriting existing client SDKs in this ticket (SDK work will be follow-ups). Major architectural changes to the serving engine internals — this is a compatibility and tooling layer project, not a runtime reimplementation.
proposal: - Versioning: Keep semver numbers for consumers but add 'capability tags' (cap:<short-name>@<minor>) that enumerate opt-in/opt-out behavioral deltas (example: cap=kv-cache-atomic@2). - Channels: Map LTS->minor guarantees (LTS tracks minor n.x with patch compatibility guarantees for behaviorally non-breaking patches). - Compatibility matrix: Generate a JSON artifact for each release listing capabilities present, tolerated breaking toggles, and recommended fallback behavior. - Negotiation: Clients may send 'Redwood-Accept-Capabilities' header; server responds with 'Redwood-Served-Capabilities' and optional 'Redwood-Fallback-To' header indicating the closest compatible version or shim URL. - Rollout gates: Gate major/minor changes by a telemetry-driven canary: error % threshold, regression on eval prompt set, and latency cost delta < configured SLAs. - Tooling: Upgrade operator reads matrix, computes safe node-by-node upgrade plan, and can inject runtime feature gates to emulate older capabilities for limited traffic during migration.
compatibility_matrix_summary: The generated matrix is a flattened list: for each runtime_version -> list of capabilities (present/absent/experimental), for each capability a permitted_grace_window (time in days) and recommended_fallback (version or shim). We will publish matrices to the artifacts bucket and tag them in releases. Separate matrices for hosted/dedicated/private where networking or KMS differences exist.
rollout_gates: 1) Canary canary_ratio default 2%; 2) Acceptable regression thresholds: downstream test-suite pass rate >= 99.5% and eval quality delta <= 0.5% when compared to baseline; 3) Cost/latency guardrails: p95 latency increase < 10ms; 4) Telemetry health: error budget burn < 5% during canary; 5) Automatic rollback on critical signals. Implementation: gating logic implemented in the rollout operator with configurable thresholds per release and per customer tier.
upgrade_tooling_changes: - migration-cli: new command 'matrix-check' to validate client compatibility against a given matrix and produce suggested accept-headers and fallback sequences. - upgrade-operator: add 'matrix-aware' mode to compute upgrade waves based on capability churn. - shim-publisher: small service to serve compatibility shims (adapter binaries/config) with urls listed in the matrix. - release pipeline: emit matrix artifact and sign with release key.
migration_steps: 1) Publish initial compatibility matrix for runtime-2.0-beta; 2) Provide client negotiation header spec and reference implementation in SDKs (follow-up); 3) Roll out accept-version header on hosted first, enable matrix-aware operator in a canary cluster; 4) Create shims for top-3 breaking capabilities and publish as experimental; 5) Run cross-team dry-run with platform and solutions engineering using a private tenancy; 6) Promote to LTS mapping once canary metrics stable for 7 days.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for matrix generator and header parsing. - Integration testing: staged cluster with clients that assert correct fallback behavior when capabilities absent. - Chaos testing: random drop of capabilities and assert operator rollback. - Eval harness: automated quality checks against our canonical prompt sets for regressions. - Load test: measure p95 changes with canary at 2-20% traffic.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit the following telemetry tied to a release_tag: matrix_applied{cluster}, client_negotiation_success_rate, fallback_invocation_rate, shim_fetch_latency, canary_error_rate, cpu_gpu_cost_delta. Dashboards: per-cluster, per-customer tier, and per-capability. Alerts: above thresholds (configurable per release) trigger rollback playbooks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Clients ignore negotiation header or are slow to adopt. Mitigation: Provide server-side shims and server-provided fallback version; maintain long grace windows and clear release notes. Risk: Matrix generator divergence across hosted vs private builds. Mitigation: Bake environment tags into matrix and require artifact signing for private deployments. Risk: Overly complex capability taxonomy. Mitigation: Keep capability names short, prefer boolean stable/experimental tri-state and document deprecation windows.
decision_log: 2025-09-18: Decided to augment semver with capability tags rather than replace semver to preserve human readability.
2025-09-22: Chose to publish matrices as signed JSON artifacts in releases bucket with environment scoping.
2025-09-29: Agreed on negotiation header names: Redwood-Accept-Capabilities / Redwood-Served-Capabilities / Redwood-Fallback-To.
2025-10-01: Agreed on rollout gate defaults (2% canary, 7-day stable window for LTS promotion) pending operator config options.
comments: PM review (Sofia Lin, 2025-09-20): asked for clear story on private deployment signing and how matrix distribution works for air-gapped installs.
Design review (Oliver Grant, 2025-09-24): suggested a concise capability iconography for Console to display compatibility at a glance.
Eng review (Riley Chen, 2025-09-28): requested telemetry keys and SLO impact assessment before finalizing gates.
next_steps: 1) Finalize matrix JSON schema and sign-off API spec (owner: Miguel); 2) Implement matrix generator in release pipeline (owner: build team); 3) Prototype negotiation headers on hosted canary (owner: runtime); 4) Create shim publisher MVP and wire into upgrade operator (owner: infra squad).
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the policy, artifact schema, and operator integration. SDK adoption, Console UI, and detailed private deployment distribution are split into follow-ups to keep scope bounded. Expect cross-team working sessions in Cycle 42.
